title: 7 BORING Rentals I'd Buy First If I Lost Everything Tomorrow (Each One Pays for the Next)

idea.name: Yard sign greetings
idea.one_liner: Rent and deliver lawn letters for birthdays and milestones, charging per booking.
idea.customer: Families celebrating birthdays or milestones; realtors arranging welcome-home signs; school booster clubs.
idea.offer: Design, deliver, set up, and collect plastic letter greetings, with a 24-hour lawn rental.
idea.revenue_model: Per-booking rental, with delivery and setup included in the price.

Price the whole trip and set a delivery radius from day [music] one.
And part-timers report eight to 15 bookings a month.

idea.name: Baby gear rentals
idea.one_liner: Rent clean, suitable baby equipment to visiting families and vacation-rental hosts.
idea.customer: Families visiting grandparents and vacation-rental hosts who want equipment at a property.
idea.offer: Provide cribs, high chairs, and strollers, with local delivery and pickup; track expiration dates and avoid renting car seats with safety concerns.
idea.revenue_model: Daily rentals, often with a minimum booking period, through a platform that takes a share.

key_quotes.quote: Baby Quip, the biggest platform for this, says a basic crib rents for about $15 to $30 a day, usually with a 3-day minimum.
The platform setup fee is about $200 and you keep [music] 78% of each booking.
One provider told Business Insider she averages around $5,000 a month.
